title: Mammootty and Mohanlal's Patriot Arrives on ZEE5 June 5. Their Historic Reunion Deserved Better Than a ₹140 Crore Flop.
excerpt: Malayalam cinema's two biggest icons shared the screen for the first time in decades. The box office didn't care. Streaming might.
body:
There are movie events, and then there are once-in-a-generation movie events. **Mammootty** and **Mohanlal** — Malayalam cinema's undisputed twin pillars, between them holding six National Awards, hundreds of films, and the devotion of an entire state — sharing the screen in the same spy thriller should have been the latter. **Patriot**, directed by Mahesh Narayanan, was supposed to be that film.

It wasn't. Not at the box office, anyway.

## The Numbers Tell a Brutal Story

With a reported budget of **₹125 to ₹140 crore**, Patriot needed a massive theatrical run to break even. It didn't get one. Despite the extraordinary hype around Mammootty and Mohanlal reuniting on screen — a pairing that Malayalam cinema fans had waited decades for — the film struggled to convert excitement into ticket sales. By the time its theatrical window closed, Patriot had become one of the costliest underperformers in Malayalam cinema history.

Now, barely weeks after its theatrical run sputtered out, the makers have moved quickly to salvage the investment. **Patriot will premiere on ZEE5 on June 5, 2026**, available in its original Malayalam along with dubbed versions in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Hindi.

## What Went Wrong in Theatres

The post-mortem isn't complicated. **Patriot** arrived with impossibly high expectations — not just for a Malayalam film, but for any Indian film featuring two actors of this stature sharing the frame. Director Mahesh Narayanan (C U Soon, Malik) brought a cerebral approach to what was marketed as a spy thriller, and that tonal mismatch likely cooled walkup audiences expecting a more conventional action showcase.

There's also the reality that pan-Indian aspirations don't always translate. The film was released across five languages simultaneously, spreading the marketing budget thin without building the concentrated regional momentum that drives first-week collections.

## Why the OTT Premiere Matters for Diaspora Audiences

Here's where the calculus shifts. For **NRI audiences**, Patriot's theatrical run was often limited to a handful of screens in major North American and UK cities. Malayalam films, even starring megastars, rarely get the wide overseas theatrical distribution that Hindi blockbusters command. Many diaspora viewers simply couldn't watch it even if they wanted to.

**ZEE5's June 5 premiere** changes that equation entirely. The film becomes accessible to every subscriber worldwide — and with the Hindi dub included, it opens up to the broader Indian diaspora beyond the Malayali community.

## The Film Itself Deserves a Second Look

Strip away the box office disappointment and Patriot has genuine merits. Mahesh Narayanan's direction is visually ambitious, the geopolitical canvas is wider than most Indian spy thrillers attempt, and watching Mammootty and Mohanlal play off each other — even in a film that doesn't quite know what to do with their combined gravity — is an experience worth having.

Mohanlal comes fresh off the massive success of **Drishyam 3**, which has crossed ₹200 crore worldwide in just 10 days. Mammootty, meanwhile, remains one of the most prolific actors working in any Indian language. Their individual star power has never been in question. What Patriot ultimately proved is that putting two megastars in one film doesn't automatically double the audience — sometimes it just doubles the budget.

## The Streaming Second Life

Indian cinema has seen this pattern before. Films that underperform theatrically — from Ludo to Haseen Dillruba to Jalsa — have found massive, enthusiastic audiences on streaming platforms. Patriot, with its cerebral spy narrative and powerhouse cast, is exactly the kind of film that could become a sleeper hit on ZEE5.

For diaspora audiences who missed its brief theatrical run: **June 5 on ZEE5**. Mark it. Two of Indian cinema's greatest actors in the same film doesn't happen often. The box office got it wrong. Maybe your living room couch will get it right.

*Sources: Sacnilk, IndulgeExpress, Bollywood Hungama*
